title: Divergent medulloblastoma chromatin states disclose KDM2B as a selective dependency.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Downloaded and parsed the GEO (Gene Expression Omnibus) file lists for the two deposited series: GSE270125 has 169 files, every one a .bw (bigWig genome coverage track), 39.5 GB total, zero peak or segmentation files; GSE269909 has 32 per-sample RSEM gene tables plus three series-level matrices. I downloaded one bigWig (41 MB, Rcmb20 IgG control) and read its binary header by hand: valid bigWig v4, genome build hg38 (chr1 = 248,956,422 bp), 24 chromosomes, 305.8 Mb of covered bases, mean value 2.65. I downloaded the 23 MB RNA-seq archive and opened a counts file: columns geneID, geneSymbol, bioType, annotationLevel, count, TPM, FPKM over 60,754 genes. I opened the series-level TPM matrix: 60,754 gene rows x 18 sample columns (D283 cells, KDM2B degradation plus four rescue constructs, 3 replicates each).
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: The paper is paywalled with no PubMed Central copy, so I never saw its full text, methods or data availability statement; the abstract plus a press release are all I had. The central resource described in the abstract - six histone modifications profiled across 52 primary medulloblastoma tumours, turned into ChromHMM chromatin states such as EnhBiv (bivalent/poised enhancer) - is not in either deposited GEO series and has no accession linked from the PubMed record. The press release points to a browser portal (proteinpaint.stjude.org/MBEpi/), which returns an HTTP 403 Cloudflare challenge and offers no bulk download.

a1_downloadable.note: The two GEO series download freely with no login; I pulled a 41 MB bigWig and the 23 MB RNA-seq archive. Caveat: the paper's headline 52-primary-tumour chromatin resource is not in them and is reachable only through a Cloudflare-blocked visualisation portal.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: FAIL. The prediction target of any chromatin-state project - the ChromHMM state label per genomic bin (EnhBiv and friends) - appears in no deposited file. All 169 CUT&RUN files are .bw coverage tracks; I grepped the file list and found zero .bed, peak, or segmentation files. The label would have to be rebuilt from scratch by re-running ChromHMM, which needs aligned reads (BAM) that were not deposited either, only raw reads in SRA.

a3_inputs_present.note: Inputs exist as real files, not accession references: 169 genome-wide hg38 bigWig signal tracks. But there is no binned or promoter-level feature matrix, so every feature must be extracted from the tracks with a tool (pyBigWig) that is not installed here.

a4_units_stated.note: The RNA-seq tables label their units clearly (count, TPM, FPKM). The bigWig values do not: the GEO series record I retrieved does not state the normalisation, and the IgG track's mean of 2.65 implies some per-million or per-genome-coverage scaling that is never named, so tracks are not safely comparable across samples.

a5_enough_rows.note: FAIL at the level of independent biological units. The deposit holds 50 RNA-seq samples and 169 CUT&RUN tracks, but these come from only 8 patient-derived xenograft models and 2 cell lines (D283, DMB006) in one lab. A per-gene framing gives ~20,000 rows but still only 2 perturbation contexts, far below the ~5 held-out groups honest evaluation needs.

a6_fits_laptop.working_set: 7.2 GB (65 PDX-model bigWigs) minimum; 39.5 GB for everything
a6_fits_laptop.note: FAIL. The smallest sensible subset - the 65 bigWigs covering the 8 xenograft models - is 7.18 GB, above the ~5 GB bar, and any sequence-to-signal model over the 3.1 Gb hg38 genome needs a GPU.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: Within the deposit the counts are internally consistent: GSE270125 lists 169 samples and the file list has 169 bigWigs; GSE269909 lists 50 samples and I accounted for all 50 (32 per-sample tables plus 18 matrix columns). The paper's 52 primary tumours simply are not there, which is an absence rather than a disagreement.

a8_label_provenance.note: FAIL, and this is the decisive one. The chromatin-state label is the output of ChromHMM, a hidden Markov model run on exactly the histone-mark tracks that would be the model's features. Predicting EnhBiv from H3K4me1 and H3K27me3 signal is learning a deterministic function of the inputs, not biology - circularity and leakage-by-construction at once.

existing_models.name: BivFinder (machine and deep learning for sequence determinants of bivalent histone modifications, Communications Biology 2026)
existing_models.score_and_split: Reported to separate bivalent from monovalent genomic regions from k-mer sequence features in mouse embryonic stem cells; exact metric and split not retrieved, only the abstract-level summary.
existing_models.authors_named_unsolved: Which sequence features distinguish bivalent chromatin regions remained unclear before their work; positional specificity at bivalent-peak boundaries is flagged as newly observed rather than settled.

existing_models.name: Enformer (DNA sequence to histone ChIP, DNase/ATAC and CAGE tracks, Nature Methods 2021)
existing_models.score_and_split: Published genome-wide track prediction on held-out human and mouse chromosomes; I did not retrieve per-track numbers for histone marks.
existing_models.authors_named_unsolved: Long-range regulatory effects and cell-type-specific variant effects remain only partly captured.

existing_models.name: DeepHistone (histone modification site prediction from sequence plus chromatin accessibility)
existing_models.score_and_split: Reported accurate per-mark site prediction; split details not retrieved.

existing_models.name: Medulloblastoma subgroup classifiers from DNA methylation (support vector machine, seven-subgroup framework) and from gene expression (random forest, support vector machine, neural networks)
existing_models.score_and_split: Mean balanced accuracy ~98% and macro-averaged area under the curve 0.99 on independent validation for the methylation support vector machine, per the retrieved summary.
existing_models.authors_named_unsolved: Risk stratification within Group 3 and Group 4 rather than subgroup assignment itself.

backbone.name: AlphaGenome or Enformer (DNA sequence to functional genomic track models); scGPT/Geneformer would not apply here
backbone.hardware: A sequence-to-track head over hg38 needs a GPU; the 7.2 GB minimum bigWig working set alone exceeds the laptop budget before any modelling.
backbone.licence: AlphaGenome weights are non-commercial; Enformer is open. Both moot because the label does not exist in the deposit.

integration.partner_dataset: DepMap (gene dependency across ~1,100 cancer cell lines), joinable on gene symbol plus cell line, and GTEx/Human Protein Atlas on Ensembl gene ID; both are plausible partners for the RNA-seq side only.
integration.join_key: Ensembl gene ID (present, versioned, e.g. ENSG00000000003.14) and HGNC gene symbol, both verified as columns in the RSEM tables.
integration.bigger_question_one_sentence: Does the set of genes that respond to KDM2B loss in two medulloblastoma lines predict which other cell lines depend on KDM2B in DepMap? - a real question, but two perturbed cell lines is far too thin a training set to answer it.

controls.positive_control: Available in principle: KDM2B's own transcript must drop after knockout or degradation, and the four rescue constructs (wild type, CXXC deletion, JmjC deletion, JmjC mutation) give a built-in dose ladder any working pipeline must recover.
controls.negative_control: Label shuffling across genes is runnable on the RNA-seq matrix; the IgG CUT&RUN tracks (16 of the 169 files) are genuine assay-level negative controls.
controls.external_validation: None available that I could reach. The 52 primary tumours that would have been the external set are not deposited, and the portal holding them is blocked.

honest_claim_h3: At best this data supports: 'within two medulloblastoma cell lines from one laboratory, promoter chromatin signal measured by CUT&RUN ranks which genes change expression after KDM2B is removed' - a description of one experiment, not a model that transfers to any other tumour, cell line or laboratory.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use promoter chromatin marks to predict which genes change expression when the KDM2B enzyme is removed.
plain_idea.train_on: For each human gene, the signal of six histone marks plus Polycomb protein occupancy at its promoter, read out of genome-wide coverage tracks; about 20,000 protein-coding genes, but drawn from only 2 cell lines and 8 xenograft models (counts verified in the deposited file lists).
plain_idea.predict: The log fold change in that gene's expression after KDM2B is knocked out or chemically degraded, computed from the deposited RSEM RNA-seq tables (60,754 gene rows, counts/TPM/FPKM, 50 samples).
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Paediatric neuro-oncology groups looking for KDM2B-responsive marker genes would get a shortlist; even a failure would quantify how poorly promoter chromatin alone predicts response to losing a chromatin reader.

more_or_better_data.why: Enformer and DeepHistone were trained on hundreds of ENCODE and Roadmap cell types; this deposit adds 8 xenograft models and 2 cell lines from one laboratory. The one genuinely distinctive piece - 52 primary medulloblastoma tumours with six marks - is not downloadable.

confidence_score.why: The RNA-seq has 3 replicates per condition, enough to estimate per-gene measurement noise, but the CUT&RUN tracks are largely one per model per mark, so there is no replicate basis for confidence on the chromatin features.

models_beatable.why: Enformer (2021) and the 2026 bivalent-chromatin models are recent, open and evaluated on held-out chromosomes or independent regions; with 2 cell lines there is no route to a fair win against them.

guaranteed_improvement.why: The baseline models cannot be run on the same split because no shared evaluation target exists - our chromatin-state label does not exist at all, and the RNA-seq fold-change label is not what those models predict.

ml_idea: The project considered was: predict each gene's transcriptional response to KDM2B removal from its baseline promoter chromatin state, with a stretch goal of predicting ChromHMM chromatin states (including the paper's EnhBiv state) from DNA sequence across medulloblastoma subgroups. Both die on the deposited data: the chromatin-state label is a hidden Markov model's output computed from the same histone tracks that would be the features (circular), and the fold-change version has only 2 independent cell lines behind ~20,000 gene rows.

effort.compute_note: Estimated, not timed: 7.18 GB is the measured total of the 65 xenograft-model bigWigs from the GEO file list; 4 GB peak RAM assumes streaming bigWig bins rather than loading tracks; the 40 hours covers installing a bigWig reader, downloading, binning ~20,000 promoters across ~48 tracks, and reconciling unnamed track normalisation.

verdict_reason: Fails Part A on three counts, two of them fatal by themselves. A2: the chromatin-state label the paper is built on (EnhBiv and the other ChromHMM states) exists in no deposited file - I checked all 169 CUT&RUN files and every one is a bigWig coverage track, with zero peak or segmentation files, so the target would have to be rebuilt from alignments that were never shared. A8: even if rebuilt, that label is the output of ChromHMM run on exactly the histone tracks that would serve as features, which is circular by construction. A5/A6: the deposit covers only 8 xenograft models and 2 cell lines from one laboratory, and the minimum useful working set is 7.2 GB of genome-wide tracks. The 52 primary tumours that would have made this a real resource are not in GEO and sit behind a Cloudflare-blocked browser portal with no bulk download.
